summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with chronic pancreatitis secondary to vasculitis, was admitted for worsening abdominal pain radiating to the back, associated with nausea and vomiting. She had recently been discharged after a similar episode. Initial management included NPO status for 48 hours to reduce gastrointestinal inflammation, followed by gradual advancement to a regular diet. Pain was controlled with IV and oral hydromorphone, and she was restarted on oral medications as tolerated. A PICC line was placed for medication and nutritional support, and she received parenteral nutrition. Esophagitis and gastritis were managed with a switch to pantoprazole, and a short prednisone taper was initiated for suspected vasculitis-related pain. She improved steadily, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged for gastroenterology and nephrology.
